claims.statement: Airtable issues personal access tokens, which a user creates with chosen scopes and base or workspace access and passes as a bearer token in the Authorization header of Airtable API requests.

sources.supports: Personal access tokens should be passed with your API requests as a `Authorization: Bearer header`.
Personal Access Tokens (PATs) allow users to create multiple access tokens that allow for a wide range of access to the information held in Airtable bases.
We currently support using personal access tokens and OAuth access tokens during the authentication process.

claims.statement: Airtable states that personal access tokens are prefixed with their ID but should otherwise be treated as opaque, variable-length strings, with no reliance on a particular length or format.

sources.supports: While personal access tokens are prefixed with their ID, they should be otherwise treated as opaque, variable-length strings. In particular, do not rely on tokens having a particular length or format.

claims.statement: Two open-source scanner rule artifacts by different maintainers both treat an Airtable personal access token candidate as the literal text "pat", then 14 alphanumeric characters, then a period, then 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. This records consistency of those artifacts only; it is not the provider's format and the provider states that tokens must be treated as opaque, variable-length strings.

sources.supports: Rule "airtable-personnal-access-token" in config/gitleaks.toml: regex \b(pat[[:alnum:]]{14}\.[a-f0-9]{64})\b with keyword "airtable" (read raw at the pinned commit)
tokenPat in the airtablepersonalaccesstoken detector: the same pat + 14 alphanumeric + period + 64 lowercase hex shape, preceded by an "airtable" keyword pattern (read raw at the pinned commit)

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: The provider says not to rely on a particular length or format, so the literal "pat" prefix, 14-character part and 64-hex part are recorded only as consistency of two scanner rule artifacts (maintainers differ; whether one was derived from the other is not established). Not researched beyond existence and this consistency claim; whether the pattern is stable across newly issued tokens is unresolved.
